_what: How a file named in a tool call's input is read at this Mac's tool boundary (read-data/file-arguments.mjs, carried from Trillion-X/trillion computer/file-arguments.mjs; here only read-data/ai-setups.mjs calls it, with $file: names it makes itself). A cloud AI names a file with a string that starts with one of the `prefixes`; the bytes are read here and put in its place, so a large file never travels through the AI's context or the account's payload. `roots` are the folders a name may point into (a leading ~ is the person's home); a path outside every root, through a link that leads outside, or with a segment in `protected_names` is refused, whatever else holds. `max_bytes` bounds all the files of one call together. Editable rows: a new prefix, a root, a protected name or a different cap changes this and nothing else.

words.not_absolute: {reference} is not a full path. Name the file with its full path from the root or from ~.
words.outside_roots: {reference} is outside the folders this Mac lets a tool call name.
words.protected: {reference} names a protected file (credentials or keys) that a tool call may not name.
words.missing: {reference} is not a file on this Mac.
words.too_big: {reference} would take this call past {limit} bytes of files. Name smaller files or fewer.
words.not_text: {reference} is not text, so it is not read.
